question: Following the Commission’s decision in July 2023 to open a formal investigation1 into whether Microsoft breached EU competition rules by bundling Teams with Office 365 and Microsoft 365 and engaging in other anticompetitive practices, the Commission replied to Written Question P002171/20232 that it was ‘in the process of evaluating its antitrust procedural framework to ensure they remain fit for purpose, in light of changes in market dynamics’3.

The press reported that Microsoft’s offer in August 2023 to partially unbundle Teams from Office 365 and Microsoft 365 was criticised by complainants and other market participants, while the DirectorateGeneral for Competition had reportedly rejected the offer of similar changes, judging them as insufficient to settle the Commission’s concerns.
In February 2024, it was reported4 that Microsoft was exploring further changes related to its bundling of Teams in order to avert EU charges. 1.
Has the Commission received an updated remedies offer by Microsoft and does it plan to issue a statement of objection before the end of this mandate?
Will it consider the use of structural remedies in this case, given the systematic nature of Microsoft’s anticompetitive practices?

Will it continue pursuing robust enforcement of traditional competition law (Article 102 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union), given that the Digital Markets Act does not address the practices in question?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (6.5.2024) Concerning the first two questions, the Commission on 27 July 2023 opened a formal investigation to assess whether Microsoft may have breached EU competition rules by tying or bundling its communication and collaboration product Teams to its popular suites for businesses Office 365 and Microsoft 3651.

The investigation is ongoing and it is part of this investigation to examine what an effective remedy would be if an abuse is established. Concerning the third question, the Digital Markets Act2 is without prejudice to competition law enforcement, which remains applicable to digital markets.
The Commission will continue to ensure the application of Articles 101 and 102 of the Treaty of the Functioning of the European Union through vigorous enforcement action.
1 https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/ip_23_3991 2 Regulation (EU) 2022/1925 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 14 September 2022 on
contestable and fair markets in the digital sector and amending Directives (EU) 2019/1937 and (EU) 2020/1828 (OJ L 265, 12.10.2022, p. 1-66).
